meta.description: An interactive learning site for two years of Swift 6.0–6.4 features: a line map, real compiler output, and concurrency and ownership labs.

home.title: Two years of new features, on one map
home.lead: Six themed lines run through five release “fare zones”. Each station is one new feature: a one-sentence explanation, old-versus-new code, the compiler's real output, and sometimes a quick quiz.

home.verify: Every Swift snippet on this site is compiled or run by `swiftc` at build time. The errors and output you see are the compiler's own, unedited ({version}).

lab.conc.hopIn: ← Hops back to the main actor

sandbox.title: Ownership Sandbox
sandbox.lead: A metro ticket shouldn't be photocopyable. The `Ticket` below has a `consuming func punch()` (validating the ticket). Click a button to append a line to the program and see whether the compiler accepts or rejects it.
sandbox.noncopyable: Noncopyable: the compiler guarantees one ticket, one punch
sandbox.copyable: An ordinary copyable type: the control group
sandbox.vars: Variables and the tickets they hold
sandbox.note: Error messages are taken from real Swift {version} compiler output for the equivalent code (for example `{msg}`). A rejected line doesn't change the program's state.
sandbox.hint: Try this: click `let b = a` first, then `inspect(a)`. Then switch to “an ordinary copyable type” and compare.
sandbox.why.borrowGone: The value of {name} was already {gone}, so it can't be borrowed.
sandbox.why.redeclared: {to} is already declared. Press “{reset}” and try again.
sandbox.why.moveGone: The value of {from} was already {gone}; there's nothing left to move.
sandbox.why.punchGone: The value of {name} was already {gone}; it can't be consumed again.
sandbox.why.noCopy: A noncopyable type doesn't allow copies of any kind, including an explicit copy.
sandbox.ok.borrow: Borrowed {name}: a read-only look at ticket No.{no}. Ownership is unchanged.
sandbox.ok.move: Ownership **moved** from {from} to {to}. From now on, {from} can no longer be used.
sandbox.ok.punch: The consuming method took ownership of {name}: once punched, the ticket is reclaimed (deinit runs) and {name} can't be used again.
sandbox.ok.punchCopyable: Punched successfully. But {name} can still be used, because copyable values are copied implicitly.
sandbox.warn.copyMove: Ticket is an ordinary copyable type, so {to} got an **identical photocopied ticket**. There are now two tickets No.{no}, and each can be punched once. The compiler can't help you.
sandbox.warn.punchTwice: The same ticket got **punched twice**! A consuming method on a copyable type silently makes a copy, so the compiler doesn't stop you.
sandbox.warn.copyOp: Explicit copy succeeded: one more ticket No.{no}.
mem.title: Memory Layout
mem.lead: Store the same N elements and `[T]`, `[N of T]`, and `Span<T>` look very different in memory. Each little square is one byte, 16 bytes per row, like a hex dump. Sizes come from a real Swift {version} run on arm64.
mem.legend.hdr: Heap object header (type info, reference count, count, capacity)
mem.onStack: On the stack / inside the owning object
mem.arrow.heap: ↓ points to a separate heap allocation
mem.arrow.span: ↗ points at elements in either storage on the left; owns no memory itself
mem.fixed: no (the length is part of the type)
mem.copyView: copies only the pointer and length
quiz.title: Guess the Compiler
quiz.lead: {n} snippets: guess what Swift {version} will say. Does it compile cleanly, warn, or reject the code outright? The answers weren't written by hand; they come from really compiling each snippet at build time.
quiz.result.wrong: Not quite: the right answer is “{answer}”
quiz.final.perfect: Perfect score! You can predict the compiler now.
quiz.final.great: Impressive. You've got most of the rules.
quiz.final.good: Not bad. Review a few more stations and you'll have it.
quiz.final.retry: Study the stations below, then try again.
